{{pp-semi-indef}}
The '''MacCullagh ellipsoid''' is defined by the equation:

:<math>\frac{x^2}{A} + \frac{y^2}{B} + \frac{z^2}{C} = 2 E,</math>

where <math>E</math> is the energy and <math>x,y,z</math> are the components of the [[angular momentum]], given in body's principal reference frame, with corresponding [[moment of inertia|principal moments of inertia]] <math>A,B,C</math>. The construction of such [[Ellipsoid#Applications|ellipsoid]] was conceived by [[James MacCullagh]].<ref>On the Rotation of a Solid Body round a Fixed Point; being an account of the late Professor Mac Cullagh's Lectures on that subject. Compiled by the Rev. Samuel Haughton, Fellow of Trinity College, Dublin. [Transactions of the Royal Irish Academy, Vol. xxii. p. 139. Read April 23, 1849.]</ref>
